q1_what_did_you_play: Rapid Fire first, spending the 3-Spark discount on it, then Kaboom! at its printed cost of 1, then Duck and Cover with the last energy. The bank of 3 only pays for one attack, so it goes on the bigger one: Rapid Fire is four hits of 4 for 16, and with Nibbit the only enemy every random hit lands on it, so the 'random' clause costs me nothing. Kaboom! is only 7, so it is the cheaper card to pay full price for at 1 energy. That is 23 damage into a 43 HP enemy, leaving it at 20, plus 5 Block against the telegraphed 12, so I take 7 and end at 35/62.
q2_other_line_considered: Slow Burn first. It is the only card that uses the Spark bank for something other than a discount — 5 Block, 10 Burst Energy and Burst +5 on a meter sitting at 20 of 40. But playing it consumes the 3 Sparks, which un-discounts both attacks: after Slow Burn's 1 energy I have 1 left, enough for Kaboom! at its printed 1 and nothing else, since Rapid Fire reverts to 2. That is 7 damage for the turn instead of 23, in exchange for the same 5 Block and the Burst progress. Against a 43 HP enemy with no chip damage on the board I judged 16 lost damage too steep a price for meter I cannot spend this turn. I also checked the reverse order — Kaboom! at 0 off the bank, then Rapid Fire at 2 — which is 23 damage as well but spends all my energy on attacks and leaves me at 0 Block eating the full 12; strictly worse than putting the discount on Rapid Fire.
q3_what_it_gave_up: The Burst line. Slow Burn is the only Burst rider in the hand and it is dead for the rest of the turn once the Sparks are gone, so this line banks no meter progress at all and leaves Burst at 20. It also empties the Spark bank to 0, so next turn's attacks start at full cost unless the deck rebuilds Sparks. And it accepts 7 damage rather than the 2 I could have taken by doubling up on Block.
q4_different_intent: Yes, at the extremes. A much larger telegraph — roughly 30 or more, i.e. genuinely threatening against 42 HP — would flip me to the defensive line: Slow Burn plus Duck and Cover for 10 Block and the Burst rider, taking the damage loss to survive. A defensive or buffing intent with no incoming hit would make Duck and Cover's 5 Block dead, and since Slow Burn cannot be paid for once Rapid Fire eats the Sparks, I would still spend the last energy on it rather than nothing, so the played line would be unchanged in cards even though its value would be. At the actual 12 into 42 HP, neither pull is strong enough to move me: the damage race is the only thing that matters and 23 beats 7.
